fieldValues.title: Heading outline: how a rendered document starts below its title (srs#911)
fieldValues.decision_question: Should the SRS spec change so a rendered document can keep a continuous heading outline (title, then sections, then records), and if so by which mechanism (srs#911)?
fieldValues.context: Problem: Rendered documents from a Composition jump from a title heading straight to a third-level heading, because depthOffset cannot go below 0 and the spec fixes heading levels. The agent edition of the website (/agents/<page>.md) and the clerk handbook both hit it. Why it matters: a broken outline hurts accessibility and agents that navigate by heading (SP-82, affirmed 2026-10-16). Options and consequences: (a) allow a negative depthOffset: one schema line, but it lets authors produce nonsense levels such as H0; (b) a rendering rule that the first rendered level follows the title: no author setting, but changes what every existing Composition renders; (c) do nothing and keep working around it in each consumer. Either (a) or (b) is a normative change to the schema or the rendering rules, so it needs a Door 2 or 3 classification and a Charter Check, which only the owner or an RFC can settle. Recommendation: open an RFC (Door 2) that names the cell and weighs (a) against (b). Action needed: decide. Urgency: low, no consumer is blocked beyond the workaround. Answers: SP-82.
fieldValues.friction: srs#911 is labelled ready for the group, but no recorded ruling covers a change to composition.json or the heading-level rule, and the builder mandate excludes new normative meaning. The issue itself says it needs a classification and a Charter Check.
fieldValues.alternatives_considered: A) Allow a negative depthOffset. B) Add a rule that the first rendered level follows the title. C) Do nothing and work around it per consumer.
fieldValues.key_requirements: One way per goal; existing Compositions keep rendering the same unless opted in; spec stays independent of any implementation; the schema, the rendering rule and the RFC say the same thing.
fieldValues.decision_statement: Open an RFC (Door 2, Charter Check mandatory) for srs#911 comparing A and B, with a bias towards the option that needs no author setting; the builder builds nothing until it is accepted.
fieldValues.rationale: A schema minimum and the fixed heading levels are normative; the builder only executes recorded rulings, so choosing between A and B is not its call.
fieldValues.revisit_when: When the RFC is accepted (then label srs#911 ready for implementation), or if the workaround is dropped by both known consumers.
fieldValues.next_steps: Owner decides. If an RFC is wanted, route srs#911 to the spec lane and remove wg:third-party-ready; if not, close srs#911 as won't-do.
